title: Volunteering as a generative act and contribution to a good life in old age—support by general practice through Social Prescribing
summary: This project explores how different forms of social participation and volunteering in old age can impact health and well-being. The idea is to encourage more social involvement through medical care, specifically using an approach called "social prescribing," which isn't yet common in Germany. Instead of prescribing medications, doctors would recommend activities that help improve social connections and quality of life. The goal of the project is to understand how important social participation is for a good life in old age, how it connects to health, and how this approach can be used in family medicine. The project will result in a practical guide to help doctors identify suitable patients and address any challenges that might prevent participation. Focus group discussions will gather opinions from those affected and healthcare providers to make the approach more practical and easier to implement. This study is conducted by a subproject of the DFG research group "Medicine, Time and the Good Life" FOR 5022 (FOR TiMed_Life).
conditions: The project investigates health risk factors that are influenced by social and lifestyle factors.

interventions.name: BeG 1: First, volunteers over the age of 60 will be interviewed about their voluntary activities in extended focus group discussions, i.e., two sessions lasting 90-120 minutes each. The observation period is from February to October 2026 (quarters 4-6).

BeG 2: Secondly, former volunteers over the age of 60 will be interviewed about their voluntary activities in extended focus group discussions, i.e., on two dates lasting 90-120 minutes each. The observation period is from August 2026 to July 2027 (quarters 6-9).

BeG 3: Thirdly, people who are unable to work due to a chronic illness and who are involved in voluntary work will be interviewed about their voluntary activities in extended focus group discussions, i.e. on two dates lasting 90-120 minutes each. The observation period is from August 2027 to April 2

FachG: Fourthly, non-recurring interprofessional focus group discussions lasting 90-120 minutes will be held with professionals potentially involved in social prescribing, namely general practitioners, social workers, and volunteer coordinators. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Inclusion criteria for group BeG1:
- Age 60 or older
- Current volunteering activities
Inclusion criteria for group BeG2:
- Age 60 or older
- Former volunteering activities
Inclusion criteria for group BeG3:
- Age 18 or older
- Existing reduced earning capacity due to chronic illness
Inclusion criteria for group FachG: 
- Professional activity as a general practitioner, social worker, or in local associations and civil society structures
General inclusion criteria (apply to all four groups):
- Sufficient language skills
- Interest in the research question
- Willingness to participate in the study and consent to audio recording of the discussions
Exclusion criteria:
General exclusion criteria (apply to all four groups):
- insufficient language skills
- lack of cognitive and social ability to participate in a structured group discussion
